title: The liquidation of method: the sign 'Marx' from Engels to Piketty
description: The Liquidation of Method (#501, February 2026) argues that Marx offered a method and that its reception, from Engels through Mao, Fanon and Piketty, turned it into content, with English 'for/against' forcing it into positions while the 1857 Introduction goes untaught. It specifies a liquidation audit and a method-versus-content contrast test, and forecasts the same capture for the Semantic Economy, Autonomous Semantic Warfare and the Crimson Hexagon. From Atomism to the Semantic Condition (#488) argues the 1841 dissertation is the metaphysical core of the system, and the Autumn Notebook (#991) argues Marx's work is a retrocausal loop. The page also holds unrelated claims on memography, the retrocausal turn, Ghost Code and the training-layer sequence.

claims.statement:
The strongest proof is operational contrast. Take one contemporary object and show two treatments:


**"Marx as Content" treatment:** identity statements, political declarations, slogans, moral positioning, camp-recognition language. No new object-level knowledge produced.


**"Marx as Method" treatment:** identify the commodity form, trace the value extraction, locate the contradiction, map the mediations, specify the alienations. New structural knowledge produced.

claims.statement: Engels was the first mediator. The prefaces to Capital Volume II, Anti-Dühring, Dialectics of Nature. Engels loved Marx. Engels also systematized him — made the method more "scientific," more programmatic, more transmissible. The preposition "for" enters here: Engels speaks *for* Marx after Marx's death. "What would Marx want?" replaces "What does the method reveal?"

claims.statement: The pattern replicates globally with local swerves: Mao's "sinification of Marxism" attempted to re-ground the method in Chinese conditions — a genuine analytical move — but was itself recaptured into state doctrine. Fanon's decolonial application in *The Wretched of the Earth* preserved the method's diagnostic function while swerving from its Eurocentric content — one of the few mediations that increased rather than decreased operational precision. Each case confirms: the method survives in the swerve. It dies in the codification.

claims.statement: "Marx was right about inequality." Even the rehabilitation is content-level. It treats Marx as a pundit who made predictions about wealth gaps, not as someone who built analytical tools for understanding how value-production works structurally. Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century (2014) is the exemplary case: uses Marx's name, borrows some of his data concerns, strips the method entirely, replaces it with empirical economics. The sign is rehabilitated. The method remains buried.

statements.quote: "Marx was right about inequality." Even the rehabilitation is content-level. It treats Marx as a pundit who made predictions about wealth gaps, not as someone who built analytical tools for understanding how value-production works structurally. Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century (2014) is the exemplary case: uses Marx's name, borrows some of his data concerns, strips the method entirely, replaces it with empirical economics. It does not. Piketty explicitly positions his work as an update of Marx — the title is deliberately chosen, the inheritance is claimed. But the inheritance is of content, not of method. Piketty inherits Marx's *conclusion* (capitalism produces inequality) without inheriting Marx's *operator* (the value-form derivation that shows WHY capitalism produces inequality at the formal level).
